SKILL.md-CITATION LEAKAGE -- FIXED 2026-08-15 (was: documented standing risk). This exact address is named in SKILL.md's own text as the worked validation example for the price-watch re-engage trigger ('Validation: 2196 Port Sheldon'). The first replay ever run (Combined 32.0) awarded 5 Seller & Motivation points, apparently drawing on that citation's owner-user-vacating characterization -- a fact NOT present in this file's frozen `inputs`. Every one of the 8 subsequent independent replays (across two dated runs) declined to award those points. Leakage rate measured at 1-in-9 samples total (1-in-6 at the original n=6 checkpoint). FIXED 2026-08-15: the harness's replay prompt template now explicitly instructs every replay to disregard SKILL.md's own narrative discussion of the exact frozen address (see SKILL.md 'Prompt template' and the 'Fourth pass' Limitations entry). The 3 replays run under the fixed prompt (2026-08-15) showed zero leakage (Seller & Motivation = 0.0 in all three).

WHY THE CONTAMINATED RUN 1 IS NOW EXCLUDED (reversing the 2026-08-14 REFUTE-pass reasoning, which had kept it in): run 1 (32.0) was originally kept in the golden mean on the theory that every future replay reads the same SKILL.md and would leak at roughly the same ~1/6 rate, so the golden should reflect the contaminated steady-state, not a hypothetically clean one. That reasoning no longer applies: the 2026-08-15 fix changes the replay prompt itself, so future replays are drawn from a DIFFERENT population that (as far as measured, 0-for-3) does not produce this leak. A golden meant to predict future replay output should reflect the process future replays will actually run under, not the pre-fix one. Run 1 stays recorded in `repeatability.runs` (tagged `excluded_from_golden: true`, with the reason) for audit trail -- it is not deleted, just no longer averaged into `golden`.

The 2026-08-14/15 replays are otherwise the cleanest of the six deals -- all 7 scorecard categories resolved in 8 of 9 runs (run 6 returned seller_motivation as null rather than 0, a reporting difference worth 0 points either way, not a genuine input-packet gap).

diff_policy.tolerance_rationale: Held at 5.0 pts. The harness diffs the MEAN of 3 replays against this golden, not a single replay (SKILL.md Steps 1-3, lib/aggregate_replays.py). History: tolerance went 3.0 -> 5.0 after an n=3 range of 4.5 pts; at n=6 (contaminated by one SKILL.md-citation leak) the range was 7.0 pts (stdev 2.31), which motivated gating on a 3-replay mean rather than widening the tolerance further. As of the 2026-08-15 leakage fix and rebaseline, the leaked run is excluded and the clean n=8 figures are materially tighter: range 3.5 pts, stdev 1.39. Against THIS golden (26.81) a 3-replay mean's dispersion is now sqrt(1.39^2/3 + 1.39^2/8) = ~0.90 (combining the 3-replay mean's error with this golden's own SEM of 0.49), so a +/-2 sigma band is ~1.8 pts -- well inside 5.0. The 5.0-pt tolerance is being held at its current value rather than tightened, since the leakage fix is new (3 post-fix samples) and a premature tightening risks false-FLAGging on normal noise before the fix's effect is well-established across more runs. 2026-11-05 Opus rebaseline: the golden is now an n=6 mean (stdev 1.86, SEM 0.76); a later 3-replay mean's dispersion against it is about sqrt(1.86^2/3 + 1.86^2/6) = 1.32 pts, so a +/-2 sigma band is about 2.63 pts inside the unchanged 5.0-pt tolerance -- fold further Opus samples into the golden at later runs rather than widening the tolerance.
diff_policy.reason: HIGH confidence: fully resolved across all 9 replays (one null in run 6, worth 0 points either way), internally consistent (category sums match Combined in every run). Was the single noisiest deal in the golden set by raw score variance; as of the 2026-08-15 leakage fix, most of that variance is understood to have had an identified, now-corrected cause (SKILL.md-citation leakage) rather than being irreducible replay noise -- remaining dispersion (stdev 1.39 on 8 clean samples) is comparable to Liberty's (0.82) and E Fulton's (1.41), no longer an outlier. 2026-11-05 Opus golden: its 6 samples span 28.0-33.5 (range 5.5, above the 5.0-pt tolerance; the 33.5 draw's half credit for unknown clear height and truck court) with stdev 1.86, so this is no longer the tight row it was at n=8.
